candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a malware probability of 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP values (+0.0087 to +0.0175), so the model is unambiguous. The listed evidence is thin on cryptojacking-specific content, though. The features are generic mnemonic bigrams about stack handling and call/return structure: CALL RET (+0.017514), PUSH RET (+0.015801), CALL PUSH (+0.014587), MOV PUSH (+0.011725), LEA PUSH (+0.010193), PUSH CALL (+0.009367), POP CALL, POP PUSH, SUB PUSH, ADD PUSH, XOR PUSH, MOV LEAVE and MOV RET. These are common in ordinary compiled code. They may reflect a distinctive code layout, packing, or obfuscated call/stack glue, but they do not by themselves show mining behavior. A few arithmetic-flavored bigrams are somewhat more suggestive: CDQ MOV, LEA IDIV, SUB SBB (multi-word arithmetic or carry/borrow handling), NEG POP and XOR PUSH. Even so, they appear at very low frequencies (0.0007 to 0.034), and no hashing-style or other mining-specific instruction sequences appear in the top 20. No function names or function-level locations accompany the n-grams, so the patterns cannot be tied to a mining routine. The evidence supports the model's malware call and a suspicious structure, but it does not confirm cryptojacking specifically. The tier is therefore low-confidence.

Very common data-movement and argument-passing pattern. It contributes through its overall distribution rather than any specific behavior.

An uncommon pairing at very low frequency (0.000708). It may point to hand-written or obfuscated code, but it is inconclusive.
